precepts.text: Whosoever eateth any manner of blood, I will set my face against that soul; the life of the flesh is in the blood.
precepts.point: He that remaineth shall be for our God, a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite: as David smote the Jebusites and Solomon levied a tribute of bondservice on those left in the land, they will be our servants. No oppressor shall pass through them any more, for now have I seen with mine eyes, as God looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them.

precepts.why:
Zechariah 9:7 says “And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth”. First the scripture about blood: “whatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among you, that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood”.

“Therefore I said unto the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood”. Whoever hunts and catches a beast or fowl “shall even pour out the blood thereof, and cover it with dust.” “Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.” That includes those of you who came from Santo Domingo: you are not to be eating blood sausage, black sausage. Don't eat that.

Now look at the blood in his mouth and the abomination between his teeth. These people, these bastards in Ashdod, in the ritual they call metzitzah b'peh, remove the foreskin of the baby and put their mouth on the wound and suck the blood from it. Infants have caught herpes from it, and the rabbis in New York negotiate to keep doing it. That is an abomination from between your teeth. What the hell is wrong with you? Your mom ain't teach you nothing?

One man called them a militarized vampire nation, living on death and destruction, on blood. Ezekiel 35:5-6 says it of Esau: because thou hast had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel, “sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.” The Most High is exposing them: the bloody mattress and baby clothes in the tunnels in Brooklyn, the baby clothes and toys on Epstein Island. God will take away the blood out of his mouth.

precepts.text: When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son; much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life, by whom we have now received the atonement.
precepts.point: Christ gave himself an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour, and we are to walk in love and become the same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters. When they put you to death out here, the Lord sees it as a sacrifice on the altar; that is what the altar in Babylon represents.
precepts.why:
Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

precepts.text: Walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
precepts.point: Christ gave himself an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour, and we are to walk in love and become the same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters. When they put you to death out here, the Lord sees it as a sacrifice on the altar; that is what the altar in Babylon represents.
precepts.why:
“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

points: The life of the flesh is in the blood, and it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul. Romans 5:10-11 says when we were enemies we were reconciled by the death of his Son, and by his life we shall be saved, and we have now received the atonement. The blood of Christ is more powerful than animal sacrifice and is the platform we build on by grace.

Christ gave himself an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour, and we are to walk in love and become the same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters. When they put you to death out here, the Lord sees it as a sacrifice on the altar; that is what the altar in Babylon represents.
